outputs.L1: Embodiments of the present disclosure provide an information processing method, a mobile terminal, and a computer storage medium. The mobile terminal includes: a decoding unit configured to obtain and decode a first multimedia file to acquire multiple frames of decoded first pictures and a time parameter of the first multimedia file; a first processing unit configured to obtain a first input operation for any selected frame among the first pictures acquired by the decoding unit; a second processing unit configured to identify, in each of the other frames among the first pictures, an area corresponding to a first area of the selected frame as a respective first area, and to perform predetermined processing on areas outside the first areas of the multiple frames of first pictures to generate multiple frames of second pictures; and an encoding unit configured to encode the multiple frames of second pictures according to the time parameter to generate a second multimedia file.
outputs.L2: The disclosed implementations relate to a data-processing technique, a portable terminal, and a computer-readable storage medium. The portable terminal comprises a decoder that acquires and decodes a first multimedia file to produce a plurality of decoded first-image frames and retrieve timing information associated with that file. A first processor receives a first user operation directed to any chosen frame among the decoded first-image frames. A second processor determines, in every first-image frame other than the chosen frame, a region corresponding to a first region in the chosen frame and designates each corresponding region as that frame’s first region. The second processor then applies predefined processing to portions outside the first regions across the plurality of first-image frames, thereby producing multiple second-image frames. An encoder subsequently encodes the second-image frames based on the timing information to create a second multimedia file.
outputs.L3:
The disclosure provides an information processing method, a mobile terminal, and a computer-readable storage medium. In the method, a decoding unit decodes a first multimedia file into a plurality of picture frames and obtains a time parameter associated with the first multimedia file. A first processing unit then receives an input operation that selects a target area within a chosen picture frame.

Based on the selected target area, a second processing unit identifies corresponding areas in the remaining picture frames. The second processing unit applies predetermined processing to the portions of each picture frame located outside the selected or corresponding area. After all picture frames have been processed, an encoding unit encodes the processed picture frames according to the original time parameter, thereby generating a second multimedia file.
outputs.L4:
A mobile terminal provides a method for selectively processing a region of a multimedia file while preserving the temporal characteristics of the original file. The terminal obtains a first multimedia file and decodes the file according to its encoding format to generate a sequence of image frames. The decoding operation also identifies or retains timing information associated with the file, such as frame timestamps, frame intervals, frame rate, playback duration, and synchronization parameters.

At least one decoded frame is displayed through a user interface. The terminal receives a user input defining a selected area in the displayed frame. The area may be specified by drawing a boundary, selecting an object, positioning and resizing a selection box, or using another region-selection operation. The selected area represents a foreground region that the user wishes to preserve.

After the selected area has been identified, the terminal determines corresponding areas in the other frames of the multimedia file. This may be performed by tracking visual features, object boundaries, motion vectors, pixel characteristics, or other image information associated with the selected area. As a result, a corresponding protected region is established for each frame, even when the relevant object or area changes position, size, shape, or orientation over time.

The terminal then processes the portions of the frames located outside the selected regions. The processing may include blurring, pixelation, masking, color adjustment, replacement, filtering, compression, or another visual modification. The selected regions themselves are retained without the applied background processing, thereby preserving the appearance of the selected object or subject while modifying its surroundings. Where appropriate, boundaries between the preserved and processed portions may be smoothed or blended to reduce visible artifacts.

Once the frames have been processed, the terminal encodes them to generate a second multimedia file. The encoding is performed using timing parameters corresponding to those of the first multimedia file so that the order, display duration, frame rate, timestamps, and overall playback timing of the processed content remain consistent with the original. Audio data and other multimedia components may also be copied, synchronized, or re-encoded as necessary.

The resulting second multimedia file therefore retains the user-selected region throughout the sequence while applying the chosen processing effect to areas outside that region. This enables a mobile device to perform object-centered editing, privacy protection, background modification, or visual emphasis without materially changing the timing or playback behavior of the original multimedia file.
outputs.L5:
# The Embodiments

Embodiments are the tangible forms through which abstract ideas become visible and meaningful. Courage may be embodied by someone who speaks despite fear; compassion takes shape in an act of kindness; freedom appears in the ability to choose one’s own path. Through embodiment, values cease to be distant concepts and become part of lived experience.

The human body is also an embodiment of identity, memory, and change. Every gesture communicates something, while scars, expressions, and movements reveal fragments of a personal history. Yet embodiment extends beyond the individual. Buildings can embody cultural ideals, works of art can embody emotions, and institutions can embody the values—or contradictions—of a society.

To examine embodiments is therefore to ask how meaning acquires form. An idea is transformed when it enters the physical world: it becomes limited by circumstances, but it also gains the power to affect others. Embodiments remind us that beliefs are most persuasive not when they are merely stated, but when they are practiced, represented, and lived.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a mobile terminal that lets a user select an area in one video frame, tracks the corresponding area across other frames, processes everything outside that area, and re-encodes the result using the original timing information.
counterfactuals.output: A mobile terminal and method for processing video data are disclosed. The mobile terminal displays a frame of a video and receives a user input defining a selected area within the displayed frame. A tracking module identifies corresponding areas in other frames of the video based on the selected area. An image-processing module applies at least one processing operation to portions of the frames outside the selected and corresponding areas while preserving or differently processing the selected and corresponding areas. The processed frames are encoded to generate output video data using timing information associated with the original video, including frame presentation or synchronization timing. Accordingly, a user-selected subject or region may be maintained across multiple frames while surrounding portions of the video are modified, and the resulting video may retain the temporal characteristics of the original video.

counterfactuals.prompt: How could a mobile terminal preserve a user-selected object or region throughout a video while applying an effect to the surrounding areas? Answer in patent disclosure language.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a mobile terminal may receive a user input identifying an object or region of interest in an initial video frame. The terminal may generate an initial mask corresponding to the selected object or region and extract one or more visual features, such as color, texture, edge, shape, motion, or learned feature descriptors, associated therewith.

For each subsequent frame, the terminal may determine an updated location and boundary of the selected object or region using object tracking, optical-flow estimation, image segmentation, feature matching, or a combination thereof. The updated boundary may be represented by a temporally adjusted mask. Mask smoothing, confidence weighting, and motion prediction may be employed to reduce flicker and maintain spatial and temporal continuity. If the selected object becomes partially or fully occluded, the terminal may predict its position and subsequently reacquire the object based on stored appearance or motion information.

The terminal may define a first image area corresponding to the updated mask and a second image area corresponding to the complement of the updated mask. Pixels in the first image area may be preserved, reproduced from the source video, or subjected to a first processing operation, while pixels in the second image area may be subjected to a second processing operation. The second processing operation may include, for example, blurring, desaturation, color replacement, stylization, brightness modification, background substitution, or application of an augmented-reality effect.

A compositing module may combine the preserved first image area with the processed second image area for each frame. Boundary pixels may be blended using feathering, alpha matting, edge-aware filtering, or motion-adaptive interpolation to reduce visible discontinuities. The resulting frames may be displayed in real time, stored as an output video, or transmitted to another device. Processing may be performed locally by the mobile terminal, remotely by a server, or cooperatively between the terminal and the server.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical patent abstract for frame-by-frame multimedia processing in which a region selected in one decoded frame is matched in all remaining frames before the modified frames are encoded with the source file’s time parameter.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system for frame-by-frame multimedia processing are disclosed. A source multimedia file is decoded into a sequence of frames and associated temporal information. A region of interest is selected in a reference decoded frame, and image features representing the selected region are determined. The region is automatically matched in each remaining frame using the image features, optionally accounting for changes in position, scale, orientation, perspective, illumination, or partial occlusion. A modification is applied to the matched region in respective frames to produce modified frames. The modified frames are then encoded into an output multimedia file using a time parameter obtained from the source multimedia file, such as frame rate, presentation timestamp, decoding timestamp, or frame duration, thereby preserving temporal correspondence with the source multimedia file.
